excerpt: When an executive board asks why you rejected the cheapest janitorial bid, you need an objective, numbers-backed scorecard rather than a gut instinct. quickAnswer: To eliminate lowball bidders objectively, score all janitorial proposals on a 100-point weighted evaluation rubric: 35 points for Burdened Labor Rate & ISSA Production Math ($35–$65/hr at 3,500 sq ft/hr), 25 points for W-2 Workforce & COI Insurance Verification, 20 points for All-In Scope & Add-On Completeness (4.33 weeks/month), 10 points for Commercial Equipment Ergonomics (HEPA backpack vacuums at 66 dBA, 500-lb carts), and 10 points for SLA & Termination Flexibility. Any bid scoring under 75 points or triggering a sub-$35/hr labor red flag is disqualified.

blocks.text: How a Weighted Scoring Rubric Defends Facility Managers From Lowball Bids

Every commercial facility manager has faced the same procurement dilemma: you solicit four janitorial proposals for a 16,000 sq ft office, three reputable contractors bid between $3,400 and $3,850 per month, and an aggressive outlier bids $2,150 per month. If you simply tell the CFO or procurement director that the $2,150 quote "feels too cheap," you risk being overruled and forced to onboard a vendor that will fail within 60 days.

A weighted evaluation rubric built specifically to detect red flags in cheap cleaning quotes shifts the conversation from subjective opinion to hard facility engineering. When your scoring sheet assigns 60% of the total points to verifiable labor mathematics (3,500 sq ft/hour ISSA production ceiling and $35–$65/hour burdened W-2 wages) and statutory insurance compliance, an underfunded lowball proposal disqualifies itself on paper before contract signature.

blocks.title: Automatic Disqualification Rule for Sub-$35/Hour Implied Labor
blocks.text: Instruct your evaluation committee that any proposal whose net monthly labor fee divided by required monthly man-hours (Net Cleanable Sq Ft / 3,500 sq ft/hr x Monthly Visits) yields less than $35.00 per hour receives an automatic zero in the 35-point Labor Math category. Because a bidder cannot reach the 75-point qualification threshold without those 35 points, mathematically impossible lowball bids are eliminated cleanly.
100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Auditing Red Flags in Cheap Bids

Use this five-part weighted rubric to grade every incoming janitorial proposal side-by-side. Notice how the point weights heavily penalize common lowball shortcuts such as ghost shifting, 1099 subcontracting, and unbundled add-on traps.

blocks.text: Side-by-Side Bid Audit: How the Rubric Exposes a Lowball Proposal

To see how this weighted evaluation rubric works in a real procurement meeting, examine a 15,000 sq ft corporate office with mixed carpet and LVT flooring (1.05x mixed-floor multiplier), 4 restrooms, 2 breakrooms, and interior conference glass, cleaned 5x/week (21.65 visits/month at the 0.90x daily frequency multiplier). In the 10,000–24,999 sq ft size bracket ($0.07–$0.12/sq ft baseline), an honest all-in monthly proposal should reflect roughly 4.5 to 5.0 nightly labor hours (97.4 to 108.25 hours/month).

blocks.text: Scoring Category 4: Auditing Vacuum Ergonomics and Cart Load Capacity (10 Points)

One of the fastest physical ways to tell whether a low bid is backed by professional engineering or corner-cutting is to inspect the vendor's proposed equipment schedule. Lowball contractors cannot afford commercial backpack vacuums or structural foam transport carts, forcing their workers to push narrow residential uprights that take twice as long per square foot and cause rapid staff fatigue.

items: High-Capacity Commercial Backpack Vacuums: Award full equipment points when bidders specify proven commercial units such as the ProTeam Super Coach Pro 6 Commercial Backpack Vacuum (6-quart tank, 4-level HEPA filtration, 11.5 lb frame, and quiet 66 dBA sound level) or the ultra-lightweight Hoover Commercial C2401 Shoulder Vac Pro Backpack Vacuum (6.4-quart capacity, HEPA media filtration, 9.2 lb carry weight with a chiropractor-endorsed harness, and 66 dBA operation). Either unit enables a technician to comfortably sustain the 3,500 sq ft/hour ISSA pace without wrist or back strain.

Heavy-Duty Restock & Supply Carts: Verify that crews move bulk paper towels, can liners, and chemical caddies across your floor plate on industrial rolling stock such as the Rubbermaid Commercial Utility Service Cart 3-Shelf, rated for a 500 lb load capacity across 3 structural foam shelves on 4-inch casters with rounded wall-safe trim.

blocks.text: 4-Step Process to Present Your Weighted Rubric to Executive Leadership

items.name: Step 1: Require Mandatory Labor-Hour Disclosure in the RFP
items.text: State clearly in your RFP instructions that any proposal omitting nightly man-hours, hourly billing rates ($35–$65/hr benchmark), or W-2 Workers' Compensation documentation will receive zero points in categories 1 and 2.

items.name: Step 2: Calculate True 12-Month Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)
items.text: Add back every item the cheap quote excluded—such as 3.8 missing fifth-week visits per month (using 4.33 weeks/mo), $15–$30/visit restroom charges, $12–$25/visit breakroom detailing, and $15–$35/visit interior glass—so the CFO sees the lowball bid's true inflated annual cost.

items.name: Step 3: Verify COI Endorsements and Equipment Lists Pre-Award
items.text: Score the finalists using the 100-point table and require the top-scoring vendor to submit their live COI and on-site equipment serial/model list (HEPA backpack vacuums and utility carts) prior to contract execution.

items.name: Step 4: Bind the Winning Score to Nightly GPS & SLA Audits
items.text: Incorporate the winning bidder's committed nightly man-hours into the service agreement, requiring monthly geofenced time-clock summaries alongside every invoice.

faqs.q: How do I explain to my CFO why we rejected a janitorial quote that was 35% cheaper?
faqs.a: Show the CFO the labor-hour math and the add-on exclusion table side-by-side. Demonstrate that cleaning 15,000 sq ft plus 4 restrooms requires 4.5 labor hours per night under the ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hour standard (97.4 hours/month at 21.65 visits/month). At the minimum legal W-2 burdened rate of $35/hour, raw labor costs $3,409/month. Therefore, a $2,050/month quote either delivers only half the hours (ghost shifting) or tacks on $1,500+/month in excluded breakroom, glass, and fifth-week surcharges.

faqs.q: Why does the rubric award 25 points for W-2 workforce and COI verification?
faqs.a: In commercial real estate, hiring a janitorial broker that subcontracts to uninsured 1099 workers exposes the tenant and property owner to co-employment wage claims, unpaid overtime audits, and third-party workplace injury lawsuits. Weighting W-2 payroll status, Workers' Compensation, and a $1M/$2M General Liability COI at 25% ensures legal risk outweighs a temporary monthly discount.

faqs.q: How do lightweight HEPA backpack vacuums affect a vendor's rubric score?
faqs.a: Ergonomic backpack vacuums weighing 9.2 to 11.5 lb with 6.0 to 6.4-quart capacities and 66 dBA sound ratings allow cleaners to cover open carpet and cubicles more than twice as fast as residential upright vacuums while trapping fine dust inside HEPA media. If a lowball vendor equips crews with cheap uprights, their technicians physically cannot achieve the 3,500 sq ft/hour production rate.

faqs.q: Should we disqualify a vendor for quoting on a 4-week month if their hourly rate is fair?
faqs.a: If a vendor's burdened hourly rate ($35–$65/hour) and nightly labor hours are accurate, a 4-week (20-visit) quote does not require automatic disqualification—provided you recalculate their per-visit price across the true 4.33-week calendar month (21.65 visits/month for 5x/week) before comparing their total monthly price against competitors.
